claim: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is a monogenic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene.
source: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is a monogenic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, resulting in defective CFTR-mediated chloride and bicarbonate transport, with dysregulation of epithelial sodium channels (ENaC).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about CF stated in the abstract and supported by scientific consensus.

claim: CF-associated mutations result in defective CFTR-mediated chloride and bicarbonate transport.
source: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is a monogenic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, resulting in defective CFTR-mediated chloride and bicarbonate transport, with dysregulation of epithelial sodium channels (ENaC).
evidence: This is stated as a direct consequence of CFTR mutations in the abstract and is established knowledge.

claim: CF-associated mutations result in dysregulation of epithelial sodium channels (ENaC).
source: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is a monogenic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, resulting in defective CFTR-mediated chloride and bicarbonate transport, with dysregulation of epithelial sodium channels (ENaC).
evidence: This is stated as a direct consequence of CFTR mutations in the abstract and is established knowledge.

claim: IL-18 levels are increased in monocytes with CF-associated mutations.

claim: Pretreatment with NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors reverses the enhanced proinflammatory signature in CF.
source: these differences were reversed by pretreatment with NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors and notably, inhibition of amiloride-sensitive sodium (Na+) channels.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: Inhibition of amiloride-sensitive sodium (Na+) channels reverses the enhanced proinflammatory signature in CF.
source: these differences were reversed by pretreatment with NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors and notably, inhibition of amiloride-sensitive sodium (Na+) channels.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: Overexpression of β-ENaC increases NLRP3-mediated inflammation in the absence of CFTR dysfunction.
source: Overexpression of β-ENaC, in the absence of CFTR dysfunction, increased NLRP3-mediated inflammation, indicating that dysregulated, ENaC-dependent signalling may drive exaggerated inflammatory responses in CF.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Dysregulated ENaC-dependent signalling may drive exaggerated inflammatory responses in CF.
source: Overexpression of β-ENaC, in the absence of CFTR dysfunction, increased NLRP3-mediated inflammation, indicating that dysregulated, ENaC-dependent signalling may drive exaggerated inflammatory responses in CF.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the β-ENaC overexpression experiment.

claim: Sodium plays a role in modulating NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
source: These data support a role for sodium in modulating NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: CF is the most common life-threatening autosomal recessive disease to affect Caucasian populations.
source: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is the most common life-threatening autosomal recessive disease to affect Caucasian populations.
evidence: This is a well-established epidemiological fact stated in the introduction.

claim: The most common CFTR mutation (ΔF508/ΔF508) results in inadequate processing of the protein and subsequent intracellular trapping in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: Mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) result in reduced expression and function of the CFTR with the most common mutation (ΔF508/ΔF508) resulting in inadequate processing of the protein and subsequent intracellular trapping in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Elborn, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to Elborn, 2016.

claim: Clinical manifestations of CF include repeated pulmonary infections.
source: Clinical manifestations of this debilitating condition include repeated pulmonary infections, innate immune-driven episodes of inflammation and inflammatory arthritis (Elborn, 2016; Whitsett and Alenghat, 2015; Bals et al., 1999; Montgomery et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Clinical manifestations of CF include innate immune-driven episodes of inflammation.
source: Clinical manifestations of this debilitating condition include repeated pulmonary infections, innate immune-driven episodes of inflammation and inflammatory arthritis (Elborn, 2016; Whitsett and Alenghat, 2015; Bals et al., 1999; Montgomery et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Clinical manifestations of CF include inflammatory arthritis.
source: Clinical manifestations of this debilitating condition include repeated pulmonary infections, innate immune-driven episodes of inflammation and inflammatory arthritis (Elborn, 2016; Whitsett and Alenghat, 2015; Bals et al., 1999; Montgomery et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: CFTR functions as an anion channel, conducting chloride (Cl-) and bicarbonate (HCO3-) ions.
source: The CFTR protein is widely expressed in a variety of cells and tissues where it functions as an anion channel, conducting chloride (Cl-) and bicarbonate (HCO3-) ions, and as a regulator of a range of epithelial transport proteins, including the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) (König et al., 2002; Konstas et al., 2003; Kunzelmann, 2003; Berdiev et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: CFTR functions as a regulator of a range of epithelial transport proteins, including ENaC.
source: The CFTR protein is widely expressed in a variety of cells and tissues where it functions as an anion channel, conducting chloride (Cl-) and bicarbonate (HCO3-) ions, and as a regulator of a range of epithelial transport proteins, including the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) (König et al., 2002; Konstas et al., 2003; Kunzelmann, 2003; Berdiev et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: IL-18 secretion was upregulated in CF-associated mutant cell lines IB3-1 (p<0.0001) and CuFi-1 (p<0.0001) relative to the BEAS-2B control when stimulated with LPS followed by ATP.
source: However, when HBECs were stimulated with LPS, followed by ATP, a specific NLRP3 inflammasome activating signal that nucleates NLRP3 assembly with ASC, pyrin and caspase-1, IL-18 secretion was upregulated in CF-associated mutant cell lines, IB3-1 (p<0.0001) and CuFi-1 (p<0.0001) relative to the BEAS-2B control.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Pretreatment with MCC950, OxPAPC, or YVAD reduced IL-18 secretion in CF-associated mutant HBEC lines.
source: When these cells were pre-treated with small molecule inhibitors of the NLRP3 inflammasome signalling pathway (MCC950; NLRP3, OxPAPC;TLR4, YVAD;caspases), IL-18 secretion was reduced (Figure 1B) in the CF-associated mutant HBEC lines thereby confirming NLRP3 inflammasome as the source of the elevated IL-18 inflammatory cytokine.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome is the source of elevated IL-18 inflammatory cytokine in CF-associated mutant HBEC lines.
source: When these cells were pre-treated with small molecule inhibitors of the NLRP3 inflammasome signalling pathway (MCC950; NLRP3, OxPAPC;TLR4, YVAD;caspases), IL-18 secretion was reduced (Figure 1B) in the CF-associated mutant HBEC lines thereby confirming NLRP3 inflammasome as the source of the elevated IL-18 inflammatory cytokine.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the inhibitor experiments.

claim: Caspase-1 activation was elevated in CF-associated mutant HBEC lines relative to control post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro.
source: Consistent with increased IL-18 cytokine levels, caspase-1 activation was also elevated in the CF-associated mutant HBEC lines relative to control post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro, and was depleted by MCC950 pre-treatment (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: MCC950 pre-treatment depleted caspase-1 activation in CF-associated mutant HBEC lines.
source: Consistent with increased IL-18 cytokine levels, caspase-1 activation was also elevated in the CF-associated mutant HBEC lines relative to control post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro, and was depleted by MCC950 pre-treatment (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Elevated pyroptosis was present after LPS and ATP stimulation in the HBEC line IB3-1.
source: Elevated pyroptosis was present after LPS and ATP stimulation in the HBEC line IB3-1 (Figure 1D), consistent with an NLRP3-mediated hyper-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: There was no significant difference in IL-18 and IL-1β secretion between HC and CF monocytes under basal conditions.
source: Under basal conditions primary monocytes, isolated from HC and CF, showed no significant difference in the secretion of IL-18 and IL-1β cytokines (Figure 2A,B)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: There was no statistical difference between HC and CF in LPS mediated activation of inflammasomes NLRC4, pyrin and AIM-2.
source: As with the HBECs, there was also no statistical difference between HC and CF in LPS mediated activation of inflammasomes, NLRC4, pyrin and AIM-2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section referring to data in Figure 2.

claim: Hyper-responsiveness in IL-18 (p<0.0001) secretion was observed in CF monocytes relative to HC when stimulated with LPS followed by ATP.
source: In primary monocytes stimulated with LPS, followed by ATP to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, we observed hyper-responsiveness in IL-18 (p<0.0001) and IL-1β (p=0.0009) secretion in CF monocytes relative to HC.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Hyper-responsiveness in IL-1β (p=0.0009) secretion was observed in CF monocytes relative to HC when stimulated with LPS followed by ATP.
source: In primary monocytes stimulated with LPS, followed by ATP to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, we observed hyper-responsiveness in IL-18 (p<0.0001) and IL-1β (p=0.0009) secretion in CF monocytes relative to HC.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Pretreatment with MCC950, OxPAPC, or YVAD significantly abrogated IL-18 and IL-1β secretion in monocytes across all patient groups (HC, CF, SAID and NCFB).
source: When these cells were pretreated with NLRP3 inflammasome pathway inhibitors (MCC950; NLRP3, OxPAPC;TLR4, YVAD;caspase-1), their secretions were significantly abrogated across all patient groups (HC, CF, SAID and NCFB) (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: IFN-γ gene expression and secretion were increased post-NLRP3-inflammasome activation in PBMCs from patients with CF compared to HC.
source: Downstream, IL-18 acts on NK and T-cells to express and secrete IFN-γ (Kim et al., 2015); we monitored IFN-γ gene expression and secretion and found they were increased, post-NLRP3-inflammasome activation, in PBMCs from patients with CF compared to HC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Elevated pyroptosis was present after LPS and ATP stimulation in monocytes from patients with CF and SAID.
source: Elevated pyroptosis was present after LPS and ATP stimulation in monocytes from patients with CF, and also in those diagnosed with SAID.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Caspase-1-independent necrosis was elevated in CF and SAID monocytes.
source: Notably, caspase-1-independent necrosis was also elevated in CF and SAID monocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2E (though the text says 2E, the figure reference appears to be 2G based on context).

claim: ASC-specks were elevated in stimulated monocytes from patients with CF-associated mutations and SAID.
source: ASC-specks were elevated in stimulated monocytes from patients with CF-associated mutations, and also in those diagnosed with SAID (Figure 2F), and were reduced with MCC950 treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: MCC950 treatment reduced ASC-specks in stimulated monocytes from patients with CF-associated mutations and SAID.
source: ASC-specks were elevated in stimulated monocytes from patients with CF-associated mutations, and also in those diagnosed with SAID (Figure 2F), and were reduced with MCC950 treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Caspase-1 activation was elevated in CF and SAID monocytes post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro.
source: Similar to HBECs, caspase-1 activation was also elevated in CF and SAID monocytes, post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro, and were depleted by MCC950 pretreatment in the monocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: MCC950 pretreatment depleted caspase-1 activation in CF and SAID monocytes.
source: Similar to HBECs, caspase-1 activation was also elevated in CF and SAID monocytes, post-LPS and ATP stimulation in vitro, and were depleted by MCC950 pretreatment in the monocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Serum IL-18 levels were significantly elevated (p=0.0064) in CF samples compared to HC.
source: Serum IL-18 (p=0.0064), IL-1β (p<0.0001) and IL-1Ra (p<0.0001) levels were all significantly elevated in CF samples, with levels comparable to SAIDs (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Serum IL-1β levels were significantly elevated (p<0.0001) in CF samples compared to HC.
source: Serum IL-18 (p=0.0064), IL-1β (p<0.0001) and IL-1Ra (p<0.0001) levels were all significantly elevated in CF samples, with levels comparable to SAIDs (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Serum IL-1Ra levels were significantly elevated (p<0.0001) in CF samples compared to HC.
source: Serum IL-18 (p=0.0064), IL-1β (p<0.0001) and IL-1Ra (p<0.0001) levels were all significantly elevated in CF samples, with levels comparable to SAIDs (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Serum IL-18, IL-1β and IL-1Ra levels in CF samples were comparable to SAID samples.
source: Serum IL-18 (p=0.0064), IL-1β (p<0.0001) and IL-1Ra (p<0.0001) levels were all significantly elevated in CF samples, with levels comparable to SAIDs (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: TNF and IL-6 were not significantly elevated in patients with CF.
source: However, in contrast to IL-1-type cytokines, the inflammasome-independent cytokines, TNF and IL-6, were not significantly elevated in patients with CF whereas the levels of these two cytokines were significantly elevated in samples from patients with SAID (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: TNF and IL-6 levels were significantly elevated in samples from patients with SAID.
source: However, in contrast to IL-1-type cytokines, the inflammasome-independent cytokines, TNF and IL-6, were not significantly elevated in patients with CF whereas the levels of these two cytokines were significantly elevated in samples from patients with SAID (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ASC-specks were significantly elevated (p=0.0007) in CF sera compared to HC.
source: ASC-specks were significantly elevated in CF (p=0.0007) and SAID sera compared to HC (Figure 3D), reflecting inflammasome-mediated inflammation and pyroptosis (Franklin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ASC-specks were significantly elevated in SAID sera compared to HC.
source: ASC-specks were significantly elevated in CF (p=0.0007) and SAID sera compared to HC (Figure 3D), reflecting inflammasome-mediated inflammation and pyroptosis (Franklin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Caspase-1 activity was significantly elevated in CF serum samples compared to NCFB and HC.
source: The activity of caspase-1, the rate-limiting factor in the activation of all inflammasomes (Mariathasan et al., 2006), was significantly elevated in CF and SAID serum samples compared to NCFB and HC (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Caspase-1 activity was significantly elevated in SAID serum samples compared to NCFB and HC.
source: The activity of caspase-1, the rate-limiting factor in the activation of all inflammasomes (Mariathasan et al., 2006), was significantly elevated in CF and SAID serum samples compared to NCFB and HC (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Intracellular Na+ levels were significantly higher (p<0.0001) in CF monocytes at the peak of Na+ influx following ATP stimulation.
source: We found that intracellular Na+ levels were significantly higher in CF cells [monocytes (p<0.0001), HBEC (p<0.0001)], at the peak of Na+ influx, which was recorded immediately following stimulus with ATP.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Intracellular Na+ levels were significantly higher (p<0.0001) in CF HBEC at the peak of Na+ influx following ATP stimulation.
source: We found that intracellular Na+ levels were significantly higher in CF cells [monocytes (p<0.0001), HBEC (p<0.0001)], at the peak of Na+ influx, which was recorded immediately following stimulus with ATP.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Intracellular K+ reduction was greater (p<0.0001) in CF monocytes upon ATP stimulation.
source: This corresponded with a superior reduction in intracellular K+ [monocytes (p<0.0001), HBEC (p<0.0001)], suggestive of greater K+ efflux in these cells, upon ATP stimulation (Figure 4A,B,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Intracellular K+ reduction was greater (p<0.0001) in CF HBEC upon ATP stimulation.
source: This corresponded with a superior reduction in intracellular K+ [monocytes (p<0.0001), HBEC (p<0.0001)], suggestive of greater K+ efflux in these cells, upon ATP stimulation (Figure 4A,B,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: ENaC inhibition with amiloride significantly reduced the magnitude of Na+ and K+ fluxes in CF cells.
source: The magnitude of the observed Na+ and K+ fluxes was significantly reduced by ENaC inhibition (using both amiloride and the SPLUNC1-derived peptide, S18, a highly stable and specific small molecule inhibitor of ENaC channels).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B,E,F.

claim: ENaC inhibition with S18 peptide significantly reduced the magnitude of Na+ and K+ fluxes in CF cells.
source: The magnitude of the observed Na+ and K+ fluxes was significantly reduced by ENaC inhibition (using both amiloride and the SPLUNC1-derived peptide, S18, a highly stable and specific small molecule inhibitor of ENaC channels).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B,E,F.

claim: Pretreatment with EIPA reduced intracellular Na+ and increased intracellular K+ in CF monocytes and HBEC lines, but not to the same extent as amiloride or S18.
source: Pretreatment with 5-(N-ethyl-N-isopropyl)-amiloride, EIPA, a broad-spectrum Na+ channel inhibitor with lower potency for ENaC, also reduced intracellular Na+ and increased intracellular K+ in CF monocytes and HBEC lines, but not to the same extent as amiloride or S18 (Figure 4A,B,E,F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ouabain treatment was associated with higher intracellular Na+ in CF cells compared to HC.
source: To corroborate our findings, we used ouabain, a Na+/K+-ATPase inhibitor, which was associated with a higher intracellular Na+ in CF cells compared to HC.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Higher intracellular Na+ levels in CF, mainly driven by ENaC, predispose cells to a greater K+ efflux upon stimulation with ATP.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that higher intracellular Na+ levels in CF, mainly driven by ENaC, predispose cells to a greater K+ efflux upon stimulation with ATP.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the ionic flux experiments.

claim: β-ENaC protein expression was significantly increased in CuFi-1 and CuFi-4 cells relative to BEAS-2B control (p=<0.05).
source: As inhibition of ENaC activity (by amiloride and S18) modulated elevated intracellular Na+ levels in cells with CF-associated mutations, we measured β-ENaC protein expression in HBEC lines and found significantly increased expression, in CuFi-1 and CuFi-4 cells relative to BEAS-2B control (p=<0.05) (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: β-ENaC protein levels were significantly increased in CF monocytes compared to HC (p=<0.05).
source: Furthermore, the β-ENaC gene was expressed in monocytes with a significant increase in β-ENaC protein levels noted in CF monocytes compared to HC (p=<0.05) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Amiloride alleviated the augmented IL-18 secretion (p=0.0001) in primary CF monocytes.
source: Notably, amiloride alleviated the augmented cytokine secretion, as well as caspase-1 activity in both primary CF monocytes (IL-18 p=0.0001; IL-1β p=0.0272) and HBEC lines (Figure 5A,B,E) (Montgomery et al., 2017; Fritzsching et al., 2015; Mall et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Amiloride alleviated the augmented IL-1β secretion (p=0.0272) in primary CF monocytes.
source: Notably, amiloride alleviated the augmented cytokine secretion, as well as caspase-1 activity in both primary CF monocytes (IL-18 p=0.0001; IL-1β p=0.0272) and HBEC lines (Figure 5A,B,E) (Montgomery et al., 2017; Fritzsching et al., 2015; Mall et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Amiloride alleviated caspase-1 activity in primary CF monocytes and HBEC lines.
source: Notably, amiloride alleviated the augmented cytokine secretion, as well as caspase-1 activity in both primary CF monocytes (IL-18 p=0.0001; IL-1β p=0.0272) and HBEC lines (Figure 5A,B,E) (Montgomery et al., 2017; Fritzsching et al., 2015; Mall et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5C,E.

claim: S18 potently inhibited IL-18 secretion (p=0.0052) exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations.
source: S18 potently inhibited cytokine secretion (IL-18 p=0.0052; IL-1β p=0.0100) and caspase-1 activity exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: S18 potently inhibited IL-1β secretion (p=0.0100) exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations.
source: S18 potently inhibited cytokine secretion (IL-18 p=0.0052; IL-1β p=0.0100) and caspase-1 activity exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: S18 potently inhibited caspase-1 activity exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations.
source: S18 potently inhibited cytokine secretion (IL-18 p=0.0052; IL-1β p=0.0100) and caspase-1 activity exclusively in cells with CF-associated mutations (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: EIPA had no effect on cytokine secretion or caspase-1 activity in CF cells.
source: whereas EIPA had no effect (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C,D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Amiloride (p<0.0001) inhibited ASC-speck formation in CF monocytes.
source: To corroborate these findings, both amiloride (p<0.0001) and S18 (p=0003) inhibited ASC-speck formation in CF monocytes (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: S18 (p=0.0003) inhibited ASC-speck formation in CF monocytes.
source: To corroborate these findings, both amiloride (p<0.0001) and S18 (p=0003) inhibited ASC-speck formation in CF monocytes (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Inhibition of amiloride-sensitive channels did not modulate TNF levels.
source: and finally, inhibition of amiloride-sensitive channels did not modulate TNF levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F), suggestive of a specific ENaC-NLRP3 axis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Overexpression of β-ENaC induced elevated IL-18 secretion at baseline in BEAS-2B cells (p=0.0003).
source: Overexpression of β-ENaC induced elevated IL-18 secretion at baseline and after LPS and ATP stimulation (p=0.0003) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Overexpression of β-ENaC induced elevated IL-18 secretion after LPS and ATP stimulation in BEAS-2B cells (p=0.0003).
source: Overexpression of β-ENaC induced elevated IL-18 secretion at baseline and after LPS and ATP stimulation (p=0.0003) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Excessive ENaC-mediated Na+ influx intrinsically drives NLRP3 inflammasome activation in CF.
source: These data support the hypothesis that excessive ENaC-mediated Na+ influx intrinsically drives NLRP3 inflammasome activation in CF.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the β-ENaC overexpression experiment.

claim: IL-1-type cytokines were elevated in both monocytes and serum of patients with CF.
source: Here we have described our findings that IL-1-type cytokines were elevated in both monocytes and serum of patients with CF, but two of the major inflammasome-independent cytokines, TNF and IL-6, were not significantly elevated in these patients.
evidence: This is stated as a summary finding in the discussion.

claim: TNF and IL-6 were not significantly elevated in patients with CF.
source: Here we have described our findings that IL-1-type cytokines were elevated in both monocytes and serum of patients with CF, but two of the major inflammasome-independent cytokines, TNF and IL-6, were not significantly elevated in these patients.
evidence: This is stated as a summary finding in the discussion.

claim: The proinflammatory cytokine response in CF has a predominant NLRP3 inflammasome constitution.
source: In contrast to patients with SAID, these data suggest that the proinflammatory cytokine response in CF has a predominant NLRP3 inflammasome constitution.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the discussion based on the cytokine profile data.

claim: There is a molecular link between enhanced ENaC-dependent Na+ influx and exacerbated NLRP3 inflammasome activation in CF.
source: Perhaps the most notable feature is the uncovering of a molecular link between enhanced ENaC-dependent Na+ influx, observed in cells with CF-associated mutations, and the exacerbated NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the discussion.

claim: Pretreating cells with CF-associated mutations with small molecule inhibitors of ENaC diminished the exaggerated IL-1-type cytokine response in vitro.
source: By pretreating these cells with CF-associated mutations with small molecule inhibitors of ENaC, the exaggerated IL-1-type cytokine response in vitro was diminished (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the discussion and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: IL-18 is the predominant cytokine secreted by non-myeloid cells capable of having activated inflammasomes.
source: In general, IL-18 is the predominant cytokine secreted by non-myeloid cells, which are also capable of having activated inflammasomes (Okazawa et al., 2004).
